title: trend-stabilized-region-arbiter-percentile-smoothing-and-fallback-plans
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Goal: Implement a trend-stabilized region selection arbiter that combines recent latency percentiles (p50/p95) with a lightweight network health score and uses a smoothing/hysteresis layer to avoid flapping. When a region fails health checks or latency deteriorates, routing should gracefully fail over to configured model variants (smaller-context or quantized) and alternative regions while preserving SLOs and minimizing cost impact.

This ticket covers algorithm design, telemetry queries, config surface in the routing policy proto, implementation of percentile smoothing (EWMA + windowed percentiles), network-health composite inputs, unit/integration tests, and a staged rollout plan (shadow -> canary -> gradual shift).
acceptance_criteria:
1) The arbiter produces a single ranked list of candidate regions for each model route given a time-bounded request trace.
2) Rankings use p50 and p95 with configurable weights, and a network-health scalar (0-1) that penalizes regions with packet loss or control-plane errors.
3) Percentile smoothing prevents more than 1 route change per 120s for a given customer route unless severe degradation occurs.
4) Fallback behavior: when primary region is degraded, route to same-region variant (quantized or small-context) first, then to next-best region; fallbacks must be observable in Console and emit events.
5) End-to-end integration tests covering simulated latency spikes, DNS/network partitions, and model-variant unavailability.
6) Shadow experiments must show stable ranking vs baseline over 24h before canary.
7) Documentation and console config exposed for operators.
design_notes:
- Scoring: score = w_p50 * norm(p50_ms) + w_p95 * norm(p95_ms) + w_net * (1 - net_health). Normalize percentiles by histogram-derived baseline (regional baseline per model and region).
- Smoothing: compute EWMA on p50 and p95 with alpha tuned per-route; additionally maintain a 5-min sliding window percentile to catch transient spikes. Use hysteresis thresholds and explicit cooldown timers to avoid oscillation.
- Net health: composite of 3 signals: control-plane error rate, packet-loss estimate (from TCP retransmits/flow-level counters), and infrastructural link penalty (reported by pop). Each signal mapped 0-1 and combined with tunable weights.
- Fallback variants: variants registered in model-catalog with tags: "quantized-8bit", "reduced-context-1k", "cpu-safe". Arbiter prefers same-region variant if latency cost within threshold, else cross-region routing.
- Observability: emit decisions as structured events (route_decision.v1) with fields region_score, chosen_variant, reason_codes, and cooldown_remaining. Console dashboard to visualize region scores + fallback events.
- Config: expose policy proto fields: percentile_weights, ewma_alpha, window_seconds, hysteresis_ms, net_health_weights, fallback_order. Default safe values provided.
- Trade-offs: stronger smoothing reduces sensitivity to real regressions; fallback-to-variant can increase model quality regressions. We'll pair with quality guard rails.
telemetry_queries: telemetry.query: p50(p95) per-region per-model over 1m/5m/15m windows using raw request latencies
compute net_health = weighted_sum(control_plane_error_rate, tcp_retransmit_rate, link_penalty) using pop-level metrics and normalize to 0-1
baseline_histogram: use 7d rolling histogram to derive normalization constants per region/model
rollout_plan: 1) Unit tests + simulation harness (local) -> PR. 2) Deploy arbiter as a feature-flagged service in staging. 3) Shadow run for 48h against 20% of routes; collect region-ranking divergence and false-positive failover rate. 4) Canary: enable active routing for non-critical test tenants (5% traffic) for 24h with quick rollback. 5) Gradual ramp to 50% over 3 days with monitoring. 6) Full enable once health signals stable and SLOs maintained. 7) Post-mortem and telemetry dashboard update.
